assertions.name: A6_pauli_identification_does_not_survive_the_lift
assertions.source: 4 magnitudes carry both parities; the two pure-parity bound channels are one of each parity

description: Discharges qou-m896's explicit caveat by lifting the (T,S) grading from the n=2 interface into the corpus's three-strands-per-nucleon construction. Exchanging two nucleons there is a BLOCK SWAP of {0,1,2} with {3,4,5} — the braid (s3 s2 s1)(s4 s3 s2)(s5 s4 s3), permutation [3,4,5,0,1,2] verified before use — not a transposition. Its spectrum across the four live H_6 blocks is seven distinct magnitudes, every eigenvalue exactly +-q^k with k in {-3,-1,2,3,5,6,9} (checked by assertion), so every L is an integer multiple of log q spanning -9 to +3. The n=2 structure of two eigenvalues q and -1/q with product -1 does NOT lift, and consequently the det T = -1 cap does not govern: bound channels have L/log q in {3,1} and unbound in {-2,-3,-5,-6,-9}, so the best |L_bound|/|L_unbound| is EXACTLY 3/2. The cap rises from 1 to 3/2 — the first thing in this arc to move it at all, every convention, crossing count and Wenzl level having left it at 1. But 3/2 still misses QCD's colour ratio of 2 by 1.33x and the nuclear 33.7 by 22.5x. And the gain is paid for: exchange parity is not locked to magnitude (q^2, q^3, q^5, q^6 each carry both signs), so the Pauli-forced identification underpinning the n=2 result is gone; the only two pure-parity BOUND channels are one of each parity, so reading T=1 as the pure symmetric channel gives a bound T=1 — exactly the failure qou-m896 fixed. Recovering the sign pattern at six strands requires choosing an unbound channel by hand.

block_swap.word: s3 s2 s1 s4 s3 s2 s5 s4 s3

caveats: THE 3/2 CAP IS OVER THE BLOCK-SWAP SPECTRUM, NOT A DERIVED PHYSICAL RATIO. It is the largest |L_bound|/|L_unbound| available from any pair of eigenvalues of this operator. Which pair a physical T=0/T=1 split would actually use is NOT determined here — that is exactly what A6 shows is no longer forced. Read 3/2 as an upper bound on what the six-strand exchange can supply, not as a prediction.

ONLY THE EXCHANGE OPERATOR IS LIFTED, NOT THE WHOLE CONSTRUCTION. This computes the spectrum of the nucleon block swap in H_6 with convention-D weights. It does not attach nucleon internal words, does not use the production bond, and does not recompute any binding energy. A full lift of qou-m896 would have to place the (T,S) grading inside the atom word itself, which remains untested.

qou-m896's RESULT IS NOT OVERTURNED — it was stated at the n=2 interface and stands there. What is discharged is its caveat: the grading does not lift cleanly. Both facts should be quoted together, since the n=2 argument's force came from the identification being Pauli-forced, and that is precisely what does not survive.
